scopeReview: IMP-6.E.1/E.2: census/survey quantities, fieldwork and narratives explaining urban change. Includes composition, fixed-boundary trends, sampling coverage, causal limits, metadata and aggregate-versus-individual interpretation.
varietyReview: Four meaningful stimuli: age-count/share table, fictional contrasting accounts, original two-series line chart and survey-coverage comparison. Additional questions apply mixed-method and source evaluation to original urban scenarios.
repetitionReview: Distinct analytical targets rather than repeated vocabulary: count/share, narrative meaning, contribution to combined growth and target-population coverage. Avoids copying earlier migration ledgers. Varied keys, detailed options and uncalibrated difficulty.
referenceNote: Official scope checked. Every count, interview account and scenario is fictional/original; no real personal data, borrowed quotations, added external resource or independent human review.

questions.correctOption: Their number rises by 100 while their share falls from 50% to 30%.
questions.independentReview: Independent arithmetic:600−500=100,500/1000=.5,600/2000=.3. Fixed boundaries/age definition supplied; composition change not attributed to one demographic mechanism.

questions.correctOption: They identify contrasting experiences and questions to investigate, without estimating citywide prevalence.
questions.independentReview: The two fictional accounts are explicitly selected, not randomly sampled; no fabricated real interview attribution or population inference. They concern different outcomes and can both be valid experiences.
Recomputed increments200/1000,combined1200,outerfraction5/6. Final Outer population share2000/3200=.625 and own growth100% are distinct distractor concepts; chart intervals equal five years.

questions.correctOption: The station survey reports 80% support and the city sample 52%, but they cover different populations and recruitment methods.
questions.independentReview: Rates independently recalculated. City sample described as a probability sample with acceptable coverage, not a census or flawless truth; larger size alone is not the justification.

questions.correctOption: Compatible census counts plus diverse resident interviews and field observations.
questions.independentReview: Mixed evidence directly matches E.1/E.2. Does not imply qualitative data are inherently unrigorous or that census totals reveal attitudes.

questions.correctOption: Spatial association does not isolate causation, and other changes may influence both patterns.
questions.independentReview: No actual business or policy effect asserted. Separates a mapped relationship from a uniquely identified causal explanation.

questions.correctOption: Evidence of place meaning that a building-condition inventory may not capture.
questions.independentReview: Fictional context, not attributed to an actual culture. Place attachment distinguished from a census estimate or universal preference.

questions.correctOption: Information linking changes to original residents, including turnover and the distribution of incomes.
questions.independentReview: Does not request identifiable student or household data. Explicitly avoids ecological inference from an aggregate mean to all individuals.

questions.correctOption: They help distinguish actual population change from differences in the time or area measured.
questions.independentReview: Kept as metadata reasoning rather than repeating a prior reclassification calculation. No false implication that all boundaries must be static if data are harmonized.

questions.correctOption: The rent is quantitative; the open description is qualitative, and both can inform a study.
questions.independentReview: Evidence type is determined by recorded information, not by whether the source is called a survey. No actual personal housing information collected.

questions.correctOption: It improves temporal comparability while combining observed landscape change with experience.
questions.independentReview: Repeated field-study case aligned to E.2; no assumption that controlled observation time eliminates every seasonality or selection concern.
